html:
Rafael Trujillo ruled the Dominican Republic from 1930 until he was assassinated in 1961, one of the longest and harshest dictatorships in Latin America.

He rose in the national guard formed under the US occupation. In power he renamed the capital Ciudad Trujillo, owned a large share of the country's sugar, land and industry, and had opponents killed at home and abroad.

In 1937 he ordered the Parsley massacre of Haitians. He paid off the foreign debt and built roads and ports. His murder of the Mirabal sisters in 1960 turned the public against him, and the next year conspirators, with help from the CIA, shot him on a coast road. His aide Joaquin Balaguer then led the country for decades.
sum: Rafael Trujillo ruled the Dominican Republic from 1930 until he was assassinated in 1961, one of the longest and harshest dictatorships in Latin America.
